The poor reference board against a round 1 medium arch_fortress threat.
The poor reference board against a round 1 medium arch_escalator threat.
The poor reference board against a round 1 medium arch_boss threat.
A round 8 hard Escalator: the fortify board wins (strength-scaled waves).

A round 9 medium Fortress: the rush board loses (the Overload decay takes its Core at tick 2800, 396 left on the Fortress's). Battle seed 2: with the neutral guards (#372) seed 1 ends with both Cores falling in the same tick, decided on the overkill rung in the party's favour.
A four-plot party (a Core and three source-barracks pairs per plot) against a round 1 easy arch_rusher stronghold of four Cores: the party wins only after destroying every Core.
The four-plot party against a round 3 boss Brood stronghold with four Cores: each Core releases one burst at 75, 50 and 25 percent of its health, a tick after it crosses the line.

The rush board against a round 1 boss Brood stronghold whose Core is set to 12 health (test override): one tick takes it from above the 75 percent line (9) to below the 50 percent line (6), so two bursts are released in that tick, highest threshold first; the 25 percent burst follows later.

The four-plot party against a Brood stronghold whose Cores are set to 7, 10, 3 and 12 health (test override): Core 2 is destroyed by a hit that crosses all three lines at once and Core 0 loses all three in one tick; the others fall in steps.

The two-plot party (three source-barracks pairs per plot) against a round 5 boss Linked Cores stronghold with two Cores sharing one pool: hits on both Cores in the same tick add up, and every Core falls in the tick the pool reaches 0.
The four-plot party against a round 5 boss Linked Cores stronghold: the lanes of all four plots feed one pool, many ticks hit several Cores at once, and all four Cores fall together.
The two-plot party against a Linked Cores stronghold whose Cores are set to 7 and 9 health (pool 16): both Cores fall in one tick and the overkill against the pool is counted once.

Time-out, rung 2: the party's Cores are given 200000 percent more health and the stronghold's Cores 6000000 each. Both sides keep both Cores, so the ladder compares Core health shares: the pool counted once (4868572 of 12000000) against the party's (1279632 of 2001000), and the party wins.

Time-out, rung 2: as the previous vector with stronghold Cores of 20000000 each; the pool keeps the larger share of its health (32868572 of 40000000) and the stronghold wins (the defender wins at the time limit).
Time-out, rung 1: the party's Cores are given 50000 percent more health (one of them falls), the stronghold's two linked Cores stand with a pool of 12000000: more Cores standing, the stronghold wins.

The rush board against a round 7 boss Pylons stronghold (one Core, three pylons of 100 health or less): the soldiers go for the pylons first (nothing aims at the Core while one stands), a pylon_destroyed event follows each pylon's building_destroyed, the last one also gives core_shield_down, and only then is the Core hit and destroyed.

The rush board with its Barracks replaced by Ranges, against the same round 7 boss Pylons stronghold: the archers (ranged, long reach) shoot the pylons from where they stand, as they would any goal, and the shield comes down before the Core is attacked.

The two-plot party against a round 7 boss Pylons stronghold with two Cores: each Core has its own three pylons, and its shield falls (core_shield_down) when its own last pylon does, at different ticks.

A party with only a Core, given 100000 percent more health (test option), against a round 1 boss Pylons stronghold: nobody attacks the pylons, so all three stand to the end, and the Overload decay (not blocked by the shield) destroys the shielded Core at tick 2400.
The same four-plot party against a round 2 medium arch_fortress stronghold with four ring sets.
The same four-plot party against a round 3 boss stronghold with four Cores.
The rush board against a round 9 boss Warlord: each wave's first unit is a Golem champion (lowest unit ID of its wave), so it leads the wave.
The rush board against a round 20 boss Warlord: the champions have 280 to 600 percent of a Golem's health (after the strength percent).
The rush reference board against a round 2 medium arch_skirmishers threat.
The rush reference board against a round 1 medium arch_swarm threat.
The poor reference board against a round 5 hard arch_skirmishers threat (it loses).
The poor reference board against a round 5 hard arch_swarm threat.
The rush reference board against a round 2 medium arch_maze threat.
The rush reference board against a round 8 medium arch_maze threat: its units walk the four-row maze through the gaps and win.
The rush reference board against a round 10 hard arch_maze threat (a long maze of 77 walls; the party's Core falls).
The rush reference board against a round 3 medium arch_focus threat, solo: every wave is plot 0 and plays as an ordinary wave.
Two plots against a round 5 medium arch_focus threat: each wave spawns only in its own plot's columns, and the plot changes from wave to wave.
Four plots against a round 6 medium arch_focus threat: one plot per wave, the cap counts two plots.
